step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify all whiteboard visual components: Deep Agent (external actor), CloudFront (CDN), Lambda@Edge Viewer Request and Origin Response, two DynamoDB tables, and an S3 bucket origin.
2. Establish node IDs and map them to standard AWS services and actor categories.
3. Trace physical lines: Agent to CloudFront ('get' request), Viewer Request Lambda@Edge to both DynamoDB tables, and bidirectional arrows between CloudFront and S3.
4. Define logical sequencing for flows starting from the agent request.

graph.name: Real-Time Statistics and Rolling Upgrades at the Edge
graph.notes: Architectural representation of Deep Instinct's real-time statistics and agent upgrade distribution using Lambda@Edge, CloudFront, DynamoDB, and S3.

nodes.name: Deep Agent
nodes.notes: Cybersecurity agent deployed on client machines requesting files and updates.

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: Caches content and routes incoming agent requests globally.

nodes.name: Lambda@Edge (Viewer Request)
nodes.notes: Intercepts agent requests to parse unique IDs, track stats, and evaluate upgrade eligibility.

nodes.name: Lambda@Edge (Origin Response)
nodes.notes: Modifies original responses from S3 before delivering them to agents.

nodes.name: DynamoDB (Statistics)
nodes.notes: Stores high-volume real-time stats extracted by the viewer request function.

nodes.name: DynamoDB (State & Rollout)
nodes.notes: Maintains state details and rate limits to coordinate rolling agent upgrades.

nodes.name: S3 Origin
nodes.notes: Houses agent upgrade packages and static software distribution files.

edges.notes: Agent sends signed GET requests containing unique identifier to CloudFront.
Viewer request function writes real-time statistics to the stats table.
Viewer request function tracks rollout state and monitors rate limits per agent.
CloudFront forwards cache-miss requests to S3 origin.
S3 returns requested assets to CloudFront.
